newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee sales rise sharply in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee sales rise sharply in latest week.

text.p: Uganda's coffee sales rose sharply last week, boosted by low prices and a rush by exporters to meet contractual obligations, industry officials said on Wednesday.
Coffee sales for the week ending last Friday rose to 93,811 60-kg bags of coffee compared to 58,340 bags exported in the previous week, the Uganda Coffee Development (UCDA) said.
"Exporters were trying to meet their earlier contracts," an UCDA official said.
Easier prices for local Kiboko and Average Fair Quality (FAQ) coffees and the start of a new season in Western Uganda also boosted the volume sold, the officials added.
Prices for Kiboko fell to an average of 700 Ugandan shillings from an average of 870 shillings last week.
"The coffee season in districts like Rukingiri and Tungamo has started and coupled with good weather, farmers can now dry their coffee easily," another official said.
Uganda exports arabica and robusta coffee. Coffee accounts for 64 percent of the country's foreign exchange earnings. ($1=1070 Ugandan shillings)
